steps.text: This looks like logon script persistence technique T1037.001 from Atomic Red Team, which is malicious - I'm examining the parent process, registry value, and the art.bat file involved.

arguments.reasoning: Identify the parent process that launched reg.exe
Identify the registry value entity written
Inspect parent process command line and its other activity
Find the art.bat logon script file and who wrote it

steps.text: I notice a file was written, probably art.bat — let me check its contents to confirm.

arguments.reasoning: Confirm cmd.exe wrote the art.bat payload

submission.reasoning: This is logon script persistence (MITRE T1037.001), matching the Atomic Red Team test. On workstation5, an interactive cmd.exe (proc-23dc9b1636) running as the user wardog wrote C:\Users\wardog\AppData\Local\Temp\art.bat at 02:46:45. At 02:47:08 the same cmd.exe launched reg.exe (proc-55d9f85e37) at High integrity. reg.exe ran 'REG ADD HKCU\Environment /v UserInitMprLogonScript /d ...\Temp\art.bat /f' and set reg-35300c4876. That value makes Windows run the batch file in the Temp folder every time the user logs on. Nothing points to a management, update or installer parent: the file is in a Temp folder and the value is a known persistence mechanism.
